case: Swamp agent/TUI application ID reuse and selective AUTOINCREMENT migration

migration_applications.semantic: applications primary key already made AUTOINCREMENT with soft-deletion and partial live posting uniqueness

company_filters_schema.semantic: company_filters current primary key is plain INTEGER PRIMARY KEY

filter_replacement.semantic: ReplaceCompanyFilters deletes all old filters and recreates them

document_gate.semantic: application lookup rejects not-found/deleted IDs before document write

document_event.semantic: document_writes uses AUTOINCREMENT as an append-only event identity

demand: Fix wrong-account draft attachment from reissued external application IDs, while avoiding schema-wide migration risk when a table's IDs are internal and routinely replaced.

structural_rivals.A0: Maintain existing targeted applications fix and do not rebuild unrelated tables without evidence of externally persistent IDs.
structural_rivals.A1: Rebuild all nine remaining integer-primary-key tables to AUTOINCREMENT in one broad migration.
structural_rivals.A2: Gate per-table migration on documented external ID references, deletion/reuse exposure, a constraint-preservation oracle and rollout-cost audit; abstain if exposure cannot be determined.

hard_boundaries: Existing P31 SQLite 48-cell result is calibration, not confirmatory evidence for this repository
Issue wording is maintainer claim not automatic proof of global absence of external references
No writes to upstream project or user databases
Do not promise historical no-reuse for IDs deleted before migration without independent historic issuance ledger
No security, privacy or data-loss guarantee from AUTOINCREMENT alone
next_gate: Prospectively freeze a source-backed functional oracle and exact pre-treatment tree for targeted versus broad migration; validate application protection, filter replacement, schema/index fidelity and migration cost on disposable copies before opening outcome.

other_independent_rivals.why: resume cursor skips records after rowid reuse; separate cursor-consistency semantics
migration 012 may already have destroyed historical issued-ID high-water; demands read-only historical impact audit before repair
ID reuse corrupts cache association despite changed rows; separate cache identity mechanism

decision: Admit Swamp source-screened R1 as first real-maintenance challenger; do not promote it beyond source-grounded candidate admission until an independently executed intervention oracle passes.
